About this item

  • MUSIC CALLS: The Bose SoundLink Flex Portable Bluetooth Speaker (2nd Gen) packs big, bold sound in a portable size that’s perfect for sharing tunes and good times anywhere on your travels
  • SOUND THAT TAKES YOU PLACES: Take advantage of the surprisingly powerful performance of this Bose wireless speaker with its clear, balanced, high-fidelity audio and deep bass that is easy to take with you
  • PERFECTLY PORTABLE, WITH BATTERY LIFE TO MATCH: This Bluetooth speaker is small enough to fit in your hand or clip onto a bag using the utility loop, plus it has up to 12 hours of battery life* so you can focus on the fun at the beach, hikes, or pool
  • TOSS IT, DROP IT, IT’S ALL GOOD: This IP67 rated Bose portable Bluetooth speaker is waterproof and dustproof and is wrapped in a durable, silicone-wrapped body to withstand drops, shocks, and rust
  • STEREO ON THE GO: Amp up the adventure with more sound when you link two compatible Bose speakers, choose Stereo Mode for left and right channels, or go for Party Mode for even bigger, bolder sound
  • PLAYS FROM ANY POSITION: Stand it up, lay it back, or hang it in the shower, this small Bluetooth speaker uses PositionIQ technology to sense the speaker orientation and automatically adjusts for the best sound possible
  • STAY CONNECTED WITH ADVANCED BLUETOOTH 5.3: This outdoor speaker uses Bluetooth 5.3 to ensure a continuous connection to your device from up to 30 feet away and can pair to multiple devices at once using multipoint technology

  • How do I connect SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) speaker to my device?

    You can connect the speaker to your device using any of the following:

    Your device’s Bluetooth settings, The Bose app or Fast Pair (Android devices only). When powered on, the speaker connects with the two most recently-connected devices.

  • How do I clear the pairing list on my SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen)?

    Flex (2nd Gen) can have up to 6 devices paired in its memory. To clear the paired devices list, turn on the speaker and press and hold the Bluetooth button for 15 seconds. You can also remove paired devices in the Bose app from the product settings.

  • Can I wirelessly link a SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) speaker with other Bose speakers?

    Yes. SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) can link with other Bose Bluetooth speakers that have a shortcut button.

    There are 2 listening options: Party Mode and Stereo Mode (Only available when both speakers are SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen).

  • What is Party Mode and how does it work?

    Party Mode lets you connect two Bose speakers to play audio in sync.

    This feature requires two Bose speakers from the list: SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen), SoundLink Max or SoundLink Plus.

    Please note, you can link to only 1 other speaker at a time.

  • What is Stereo Mode and how does it work?

    Stereo Mode allows you to unlock a stereo audio experience where the left and right speaker play separately.

    To use Stereo Mode with a SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) Speaker, a second SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) is required.

Product Description

Press play and go further with the Bose SoundLink Flex Portable Bluetooth Speaker (2nd Gen). This small portable speaker features a surprisingly big, bold sound and is perfectly portable. It‚Äôs small enough to fit in your hand, throw in your pack, or clip to the outside of your bag using the built-in nylon sport utility loop. Featuring high-fidelity audio and deep bass, the Bose SoundLink Flex Bluetooth Speaker is loud enough to fill the space wherever you are on your journey. Want to up your party tunes even further? Just use the Bose app to adjust the EQ and control other features of your Bose portable Bluetooth speaker like battery life, Bluetooth connection, shortcut customization, and more. Rigorously tested to meet an IP67 rating, this Bose Bluetooth speaker with microphone is waterproof and dustproof and can even withstand drops, crushing, shocks, and rust thanks to a tough silicone-wrapped body. Plus, this outdoor Bluetooth speaker even floats so a quick dip in the pool won‚Äôt sink your sound. Whether you place this waterproof Bluetooth speaker on a table or hang it from a backpack, PositionIQ technology automatically adjusts the speaker‚Äôs performance based on orientation to provide the best sound. With up to 12 hours of battery life* and advanced Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity‚Äî this Bose portable speaker lets you focus on the fun and keeps the dance party going into the night. Share good times anywhere on the planet with the Bose SoundLink Flex Portable Bluetooth Speaker (2nd Gen). *The SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) battery lasts up to 12 hours of play time at typical listening levels. At maximum volume, it will provide up to 3 hours of play time.

    • Preston
      5 out of 5 stars
      Best choice for indoor listening!
      Reviewed in the United States on July 30, 2026
      Color: Fog Grey
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      I bought the Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) to compare it directly against the JBL Flip 7 since they seem to be the two most popular speakers in this size category.

      For my ears, the Bose won.

      The biggest difference is the bass. The JBL has a little more punch in the mid-bass, but the Bose reaches noticeably deeper into the low end. It almost sounds like it has a tiny built-in subwoofer. That deeper bass gives music a fuller, richer sound that I really enjoy.

      Most of my listening is indoors in small to medium-sized rooms, and that's where the Bose really shines. Vocals are clear, instruments sound natural, and everything sounds balanced without being harsh. I found myself enjoying the music instead of focusing on what the speaker was doing.

      The JBL Flip 7 definitely has its strengths. It's smaller, lighter, looks better in my opinion, and is easier to throw into a backpack or even a bike bottle holder. It also projects a little better in larger rooms. If portability is your top priority, I completely understand choosing the JBL.

      For outdoor use, though, I don't think either speaker has enough low-end to really impress in wide-open spaces. Since the JBL's slight advantage in volume and projection wasn't enough to make a big difference outside, I preferred the Bose because it sounded so much better indoors.

      For reference, I came from an old Anker Soundcore Boost that finally gave up. Oddly enough, I still think the Soundcore Boost has more outright "thump" than either the JBL or the Bose. However, both of these speakers are much cleaner, clearer, and more refined overall.

      If your primary use is listening around the house, in the garage, on the patio, or in a small to medium-sized room, I think the Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) is the better-sounding speaker. If you need maximum portability for bike rides, hiking, or travel, the JBL Flip 7 may be the better fit.

      Neither speaker is bad, they're just tuned differently. For my listening preferences, the Bose was the easy winner, and it's the one I'm keeping.

      4 out of 5 stars
      Review from a Bose Fan
      Reviewed in the United States on August 25, 2026
      Color: Fog Grey
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      Note to Amazon: This is a different product than the Bose Soundlink Plus which I've reviewed also, not the same product.

      I have been a Bose fan for a long time and still use my Roommate speakers, now with a Bluetooth receiver. My Chromebook speakers need help, and a Bluetooth speaker is the solution I chose, trying, first with the Bose Plus model which does not work at all with Chromebook.

      The Flex stays connected to the laptop when the speaker is moved from room to room. The few times I've used it on the battery, it has used about half the battery in about 2 hours of listening with the volume moderately high.

      Although the sound is excellent overall at the highs and midrange, the bass is too deep or muddy, and has an echo quality. The official Bose equalizer app only works with selected devices, such as Android and Apple, not with Chromebook.

      Depending on how you use this speaker, you may want to get a USB C to A charging cord. I keep it plugged in near my laptop, and learned that on a C to C cord and C block, the unit will not refill without replugging it, but with a C to A cord and A block, it recharges as it is used.

      Ich habe mir den Bose SoundLink Flex für unterwegs und den Garten geholt – und bin absolut begeistert! Der Lautsprecher überzeugt mit kraftvollem, glasklarem Sound und einem überraschend tiefen Bass für diese kompakte Größe. Egal ob Pop, Klassik oder Podcasts – der Klang ist ausgewogen, dynamisch und einfach typisch Bose.

      Das Gerät ist wasserdicht (IP67), stoßfest und liegt super in der Hand. Perfekt für Outdoor-Aktivitäten oder einfach für die Wohnung. Auch die Akkulaufzeit ist top – ich komme locker auf 10+ Stunden bei normaler Lautstärke.

      ✅ Was mir besonders gefällt:

      Fantastischer Klang mit sattem Bass

      Sehr robust & wasserfest – ideal für draußen

      Stylisches, minimalistisches Design

      Schnelle, stabile Bluetooth-Verbindung

      Lange Akkulaufzeit und einfache Bedienung

      Ich hatte schon einige Bluetooth-Lautsprecher – aber der SoundLink Flex spielt ganz klar in einer anderen Liga. Wer Wert auf hochwertigen Klang in einem tragbaren Format legt, wird hier definitiv glücklich.

      🎧 Klare 5 Sterne – uneingeschränkte Kaufempfehlung!
